page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.55 GHz, allocating 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Hardware cache configuration features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. Instruction set support includes AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 virtual CPU to RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance includes 7 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without bundled local storage, and includes zero dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the instance predominantly within the mid-range performance tier. Multi-core compute execution shows steady throughput, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8861.0, a PassMark CPU score of 21235.7, and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 21587.12. Memory throughput presents mixed behavior: small-block cached read operations reach 1033.55 GB/sec, and large-block read-only memory bandwidth measures 39.33 GB/sec in the average bracket, whereas uncached large-block write bandwidth drops to 18.82 GB/sec, placing it in the lower 25 percent. In specialized evaluations, small-model language generation achieved a strong rating with 307.15 tokens per second for a 135M parameter model, alongside 15.73 million Redis SET operations per second.

The configuration balances execution density and general system memory, offering qualitative resource efficiency for sustained, non-bursting corporate tasks. Because local storage is absent, all persistent data workloads require external network-attached volumes. The hardware balance aligns with web application hosting, caching tiers, compilation tasks, database engines with remote storage configurations, and routine enterprise microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of memory, driven by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor at 2.55 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by KVM, it provides a consistent 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The instance provides 7 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes no bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing shows balanced middle-tier CPU capabilities across Geekbench and PassMark suites, with responsive cached read speeds but reduced uncached write memory bandwidth. It delivers 15.73 million Redis SET operations per second and handles lightweight language model generation efficiently. The server suits standard enterprise workloads, web application serving, backend microservices, and in-memory caches that do not require local NVMe storage.
